statements.statement: Total school-related receipts, assessments and charges resulted in $42,730 in increased state aid versus what the town budget was built on
Chapter 70 increase was $135,915
No change in school transportation reimbursement
Charter tuition reimbursement went up $116,413
Smart growth school reimbursement was $160,187, the majority of the state aid increase; was zero two years ago
School choice receiving tuition was $5,541, with a question outstanding on whether it counts in the net increase
School choice sending tuition charge to the town was reduced, picking up $57,000
Charter schools sending tuition charge went up; town was charged $72,000 more

Superintendent's request, reviewed with the petitioner, totaled about $350,000 across five items: primary school reading specialist, Turkey Hill reading specialist, bringing the Lunenburg vice principal to full-time, 52 Ignite online tutoring seats, and the high school music teacher position
Lunenburg High School music teacher position planned to go from .6 FTE to full-time, programmed for the second half of the year
Town and schools combined saved more than $100,000 from reconstituted health insurance plans (recurring buyouts and a high-deductible/HSA option)
Superintendent said she was comfortable the primary school reading specialist could be funded out of health insurance savings for FY27
A member asked why, with $400,000, the district didn't instead restore grade 1-4 positions to reduce class size, rather than fund the five requested items
If the $400,000 isn't passed at the special town meeting, the school district has latitude in its own budget to cover the shortfall elsewhere
Governor has also proposed a supplemental budget that could further affect Chapter 70, not confirmed
Rough calculation off a per-student figure (heard as $118 or $112) times about 1,500 students comes to about 168 (units unclear)
A member said they'd heard the net cherry sheet increase on the town side was 471
Clarified/corrected to around another $71,000 net on the town side of the cherry sheet
Unrestricted general government aid (UGGA) went up about $30,000
Veterans benefits and elderly aid line went up about $43,000
Combined UGGA plus veterans/elderly increase was almost $74,000
The school department had to reduce operations by $761,000 or $771,000 to live within the budget allocation proposed, to maintain level services
Even applying the $400,000 in new revenue, the school is still about $371,000 negative relative to level services next year
